data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Maṣriwonne baḥ ḥawle. Kətwo xəṣuṣi ḥawlo maṣriwole w kətwolle bə qḏolayye hno ʕarnoṣe, baʕ ʕarnoṣanək mxarbəqiwole w makrəxiwonne laǧan d lə makiwi aḥ ḥəyewən.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: They would tie them with ropes. There was a special rope, they would tie it, and they had, on their necks, those ʕarnoṣe [wooden yokes or clamps]; they would thread it through those clamps and make them go round, so that they would not hurt the animals.

rationale: First active Infectum-wa box; rope fastening/looping fits existing sense 2 better than tangling 1. Exact threading/knotting operation remains open. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.
